messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: HIGH - LB-PRIMARY-HEALTHDOWN fired for service 'redwood-lb-primary' in prod-eu-west. Trigger: target_health_check failures > 60s. page: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/P12345

pagerduty: Alert acknowledged by emma (oncall-sre) at 03:45 UTC. Escalation paused.

emma (oncall-sre): I'm on it, starting runbook LB-Health. First check LB target groups + TLS handshake error rates. 

mike (day-sre): I'm coming up to speed, leaving a note: night shift saw cert rotation at 03:30 UTC on primary LB. Could be related.

raj (neteng): Looking at Cloud LB console — several targets in eu-west-1 are marked unhealthy (503s), backend TLS handshake errors showing "alert handshake_failure" in the logs.

sara (eng-runtime): We just rolled out a small runtime change to tolerate 0-RTT, but that shouldn't break TLS. I'll check app logs for TLS negotiation failures.

emma (oncall-sre): Quick mitigation idea: route traffic to standby LB in eu-west-2 and set primary to draining. Initiating failover via infra playbook now. 

ops-manager: Please post estimated customer impact once confirmed. CS has already flagged at least 3 tickets.

pagerduty: Action: emma routed 60% traffic -> redwood-lb-standby (eu-west-2). Remaining 40% stayed on primary for validating rollback.

raj (neteng): Noticed DNS TTL for lb-primary.redwood.net is 300s. Some clients still resolving old IPs. Also seeing a few legacy customers pinned to IP addresses (ughh). Propagation seems partial.

emma (oncall-sre): Observed spike in TLS handshake_timeouts and SNI mismatch errors. Suspect certificate installed on LB didn't include SAN for internal clients (we rotated to new cert from KMS automatically).

sara (eng-runtime): Pulled TLS logs from backend: repeated lines: `SSL_connect: error:1408A0C1:SSL routines:ssl3_get_client_hello:no shared cipher`. Looks like cipher mismatch with a subset of clients. But majority are failing during handshake before cipher negotiation — suspicious.

emma (oncall-sre): Plan A: rollback cert to previous version on primary LB. Plan B: if rollback not immediate, shift 100% traffic to standby. Executing rollback attempt 03:58 UTC.

pagerduty: rollback attempt failed (cert not found in LB config). Fallback: update routing policy to send 100% to standby.

mike (day-sre): Routing updated, 100% now in standby (eu-west-2). Monitoring target health — backends there are green. Latency returning to normal for most customers. :relieved:

emma (oncall-sre): Confirming customer impact: error-rate on text-generation endpoints peaked at ~28% across eu-west; now down to 2% after failover. We have ~12 open CS tickets, 2 high-priority customers reported timeouts.

cust-success-bot: Notifying customer success leads and posting CIDs: #CID-4321, #CID-4322 for the two high-priority accounts.

raj (neteng): Root cause hypothesis: automated cert rotation pushed a cert lacking internal SANs to primary LB. Additionally, DNS/TLS interplay meant some clients persisted to IPs bound to the broken cert.

sara (eng-runtime): Also saw that one backend version in eu-west-1 didn't advertise the same ciphers after a rolling deploy earlier. Might have contributed to mixed handshake failures.

emma (oncall-sre): Immediate resolution: traffic diverted to healthy standby, primary put into maintenance, certificate inventory being audited. Next steps: restore primary only after cert + backend cipher parity validated.

pagerduty: Pager acknowledged: incident status set to 'Mitigated' at 04:20 UTC. Auto-escalation disabled.

ops-manager: Please prepare a short impact summary for execs: total affected requests, percent of traffic impacted, list of customers with incidents, timeframe.

emma (oncall-sre): Early impact numbers: 03:30-04:15 UTC window, ~1.2M total requests in eu-west, ~340k failed requests (28% peak, aggregated 8% over window). Will reconcile with logs and billing.

mike (day-sre): Handoff note for post-incident: I'll own the follow-up with neteng and runtime teams. We'll verify certs in KMS, add pre-rotation checks for SANs, and raise DNS TTL change guidance to reduce pinning issues.

raj (neteng): Action items for me: add a verification step in cert rotation job to confirm SANs include internal and external names; add smoke test post-rotation that attempts TLS handshake from a set of client profiles.

sara (eng-runtime): Action items: review recent runtime deploy that changed cipher list; ensure backward-compatible cipher suite is enabled; add a regression test to nightly e2e with TLS handshake vectors.

ops-manager: Also consider updating incident-bot to page on certificate rotation anomalies and to surface DNS pinning heuristics.

cust-success-bot: CS updates queued: templated email to affected accounts drafted and awaiting review.

emma (oncall-sre): Final operational note: incident declared resolved at 04:20 UTC after traffic normalized and 15min stable window. Will file postmortem and tag for P1 tracking. Handing off to mike (day-sre) for root cause/PM.

mike (day-sre): Taking ownership. Will schedule RCA with neteng & runtime and include mitigation timelines. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

pagerduty: Incident closed at 05:10 UTC by emma (oncall-sre).

incident-bot: This thread will be archived. Please add any additional notes or logs before archival.
